CNTFREQ: Maximo populates the field based on the date you enter in the Count Date field and the Count Frequency and Last Count Date values for the items in the selected storeroom. You set up the count frequency and last count date on the Inventory tab in Inventory. ICG: The value you specify must exist as an inventory count group for at least one countable item in the storeroom that you want to count. You can enter multiple ICG selection values. You can assign an inventory count group to a item manually in the Inventory application. ITEM: The item that you enter must exist as a countable item in the storeroom you are counting. You can enter multiple item selection values. ROTATING: Maximo selects only rotating items from the current storeroom.
selectiontype.title: Selection Criterion

selectionicg.description: Inventory count group. This field specifies the group of items that are in the count book. The value you specify must exist as an inventory count group for at least one countable item in the storeroom you want to count. When you choose ICG in the Selection Criterion field, you must enter at least one ICG value in the Select Items table. You can assign an inventory count group to a item manually in the Inventory application.
selectionicg.title: Selection ICG

cntfreqdate.description: Date on or before which the physical count for the items on the count book is scheduled to be completed, based on each item's  last count date and count frequency values. If you entered CNTFREQ as the selection criterion, you must enter a date in the Count Date field. You can change the count frequency and last count date for a item in Inventory. Example: If the count date is March 31, 2007, Maximo selects countable items whose count date and count frequency determine that they must be physically counted on or before March 31st. Maximo selects a item, for example, with a count frequency of 15 days and a last count date of March 10, 2007. This item was due for a physical count on March 25, 2007. Maximo does not select a item with a count frequency of 60 days and last count date of March 1, 2007. That item is not due for a physical count until May 1, 2007.
cntfreqdate.title: Count Date

selectionitm.description: Criterion that you selected for the count book in the Item Selection area of the Count Book tab. The Selection Criterion value determines whether you must enter at least one value in the Item, ICG, or Count Date fields. If the value in the Selection Criterion field is ROTATING or ALL, do not specify any values in the Select Items table. Maximo selects those countable items that meet the criterion for the storeroom being counted.

oslc.properties.name: oslc.properties

_dropnulls.name: _dropnulls
_dropnulls.description: Default value is 1. If set to 0, the json response will include attributes with null values also.

transactionid.name: transactionid
transactionid.description: This is used to prevent de-duplication for create/update/delete. If this header is present then the value is compared to a list of committed transaction ids.If it has a match, then it is considered as a duplicate transaction and an HTTP conflict error is generated.

oslc.where.name: oslc.where
oslc.where.description: Where clause to filter the set of resources

x-allow-events.name: x-allow-events
x-allow-events.description: For a create/update/delete, if the request wants to suppress the object events, this request header needs to be set to 0. By default all events are fired unless programmatically stopped.

x-method-override.name: x-method-override
x-method-override.description: Due to constraints from browser the HTTP POST method is re-used for creates and updates and deletes.This request header is used to convey the specifics of the POST request. PATCH is used for update. DELETE is used for deleting the resource. BULK is used for supporting bulk operations.If this header is not present, the POST request is treated as a create request.

gbrange.name: gbrange

lean.name: lean
lean.description: If set to 1, this will instruct the api to work with the "lean" json format as opposed to the namespaced json that it produces by default. allornothing.name: allornothing
